incidents.victim: South American and southeastern European government agencies
incidents.vector: Initial access via suspected zero-day or n-day exploitation, followed by deployment of custom NetDraft, CloudSorcerer, VSHELL and SNOWRUST implants for long-term access.
incidents.impact: Talos disclosed a multi-year campaign by China-nexus group UAT-8302 against government entities in South America since late 2024 and southeastern Europe in 2025, with credential theft, AD enumeration and lateral movement across compromised networks.

incidents.vector: Fake ScreenConnect updater drops a Rust loader that deploys the modular CloudZ .NET RAT, which uses a new Pheno plugin to abuse the Microsoft Phone Link bridge and read SMS-based one-time-password (OTP) data from the victim's phone.
incidents.impact: Talos uncovered an intrusion active since at least January 2026 in which CloudZ exfiltrates browser credentials and intercepts SMS/OTP messages from synced mobile devices, undermining MFA based on text codes.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion gaining access to internal source-code repositories.
incidents.impact: Trellix disclosed a security breach exposing portions of its source code; the Europol partner says no product changes were made and notified law enforcement.

incidents.victim: 80+ organizations across the US, Western Europe and Latin America
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — initial access broker / ransomware precursor
incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating the US Social Security Administration drive victims to a compromised site that deploys both SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect remote-monitoring tools, giving the attacker dual persistent access without traditional malware.
incidents.impact: Securonix tracks the VENOMOUS#HELPER campaign as active since at least April 2025, hitting 80+ organizations and signaling a 277% year-over-year jump in RMM-tool abuse, with evidence the operator targets executives and cryptocurrency holders.

incidents.vector: Cybercriminal intrusion into Instructure's environment with theft of customer records; Instructure responded by revoking privileged credentials, rotating tokens and deploying patches.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claimed theft of 3.6 TB of data covering more than 9,000 schools using the Canvas learning platform; Instructure confirmed names, emails, student IDs and user messages were exposed but said financial data and passwords were not.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion of CNAM database systems with no ransom demand; Moldova's cyber agency has not ruled out Russian involvement.
incidents.impact: Moldovan officials confirmed theft of personal and financial information on essentially every adult who paid into the national health insurance scheme, plus financial data on private medical providers; reports indicate roughly 30% of the database was impacted.

incidents.victim: Cuban Embassy in Washington and 5,000+ Microsoft Exchange servers
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Microsoft Exchange email servers to access mailboxes; the same actor compromised more than 5,000 Exchange servers in 2026.
incidents.impact: Chinese state-linked hackers reportedly breached the Cuban embassy in Washington to spy on the US-led naval blockade of Iran, lifting diplomatic email inboxes as part of a broader Exchange-server hacking campaign.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company and Delta Dental of New York
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (Cl0p MOVEit campaign)
incidents.vector: Threat actors exploited the 2023 MOVEit Transfer zero-day to access file-transfer servers used by Delta Dental affiliates.
incidents.impact: NYDFS announced a $2.25M settlement for inadequate incident-response and late breach reporting; the underlying 2023 incident exposed names, addresses, SSNs, driver's licenses, financial accounts and patient health information.

incidents.victim: cPanel / WHM-hosted websites (millions exposed, ~15,000 confirmed compromised)
incidents.attacker: Multiple criminal actors — ransomware and botnet operators
incidents.vector: Authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-41940 (CVSS 9.8) in cPanel/WHM session handling allows unauthenticated remote takeover and code execution; multiple working PoCs surfaced within 24 hours of disclosure.
incidents.impact: Censys observed about 15,000 compromised instances within 24 hours of disclosure, with attackers deploying Mirai botnet variants, the .sorry ransomware and defacement payloads; KnownHost confirmed in-the-wild exploitation since at least 23 February 2026 and Shadowserver counts 44,000+ already compromised cPanel systems.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely (Zhong Stealer / GoldenEyeDog links)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering attack on tech-support staff posing as customers; targets were tricked into running a malicious .SCR Windows-screensaver file, and a misconfigured CrowdStrike EDR agent allowed access to persist for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole initialization codes for in-progress EV code-signing orders and obtained 27 EV code-signing certificates, then used them to sign Zhong Stealer payloads tied to cryptocurrency theft; all 27 certificates were later revoked.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (World Leaks / ex-Hunters International)
incidents.vector: Data-theft and extortion intrusion against the publisher's environment; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: World Leaks published roughly 8.5 TB of allegedly sensitive Mediaworks data including payroll, contracts, financial statements and editorial communications; leaked memos suggest the pro-Orbán publisher coordinated anti-Ukraine messaging with Moscow contacts.

incidents.vector: Data theft from a 2026 ShinyHunters campaign that also hit Zara, 7-Eleven, Udemy and Medtronic.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 7.5 million Carnival customers was leaked online by ShinyHunters as part of a wider mass-extortion spree against major consumer brands.

incidents.vector: Compromise of an employee account used to access customer-data systems.
incidents.impact: Canada Life confirmed customer data was stolen via a compromised employee account; the company says the incident is contained and is investigating the scope of exposure.

incidents.victim: US federal civilian executive branch agencies (Cisco ASA / FTD users)
incidents.vector: APT actors exploited CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362 in Cisco ASA firmware to deploy the FIRESTARTER malware on Firepower and Secure Firewall devices, achieving persistence that survives firmware patching.
incidents.impact: CISA, NCSC-UK and ASD's ACSC issued joint guidance and updated Emergency Directive 25-03 after detecting FIRESTARTER on FCEB devices; previously patched Cisco firewalls remained compromised, prompting required forensic collection and YARA-based detection across federal and allied networks.

incidents.vector: Threat group UNC6692 followed an email-bomb 'helpdesk' lure with Microsoft Teams social engineering, tricking the victim into running an AutoHotKey loader that installed the SNOWBELT browser extension and SNOWGLAZE tunnel for AD/LSASS dumping and pass-the-hash to the domain controller.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group documented a multistage UNC6692 intrusion ('Snow Flurries') that achieved deep network penetration, dumped the NTDS.dit and SAM hives via FTK Imager and exfiltrated them via LimeWire — illustrating advanced helpdesk-impersonation tradecraft.

incidents.victim: KICS vulnerability scanner users (incl. Bitwarden CLI)
incidents.vector: Attackers pushed malicious versions of the KICS Docker image, GitHub Action and VS Code extension — the second supply-chain compromise of the Checkmarx-managed scanner in a month.
incidents.impact: Bitwarden CLI was confirmed as the first major downstream victim of the KICS supply-chain compromise; users of the KICS Docker image and integrations were exposed to attacker-controlled code.

incidents.victim: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner / German federal government
incidents.vector: Russian operators used Signal account-takeover techniques to compromise the Bundestag President's Signal account, gaining visibility into a sensitive group chat that included Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
incidents.impact: Russian cyber spies eavesdropped on a Signal group containing senior German officials including the Chancellor; Merz's own account was not breached, but Germany's BSI confirmed sustained Russian phishing of Signal/WhatsApp accounts of European officials.

incidents.vector: Funds were diverted during a foreign-debt repayment workflow; Australian law enforcement is assisting with attribution.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole $2.5 million from a debt repayment intended for Australia, prompting cross-border investigation.

incidents.vector: Data-theft incident with stolen records subsequently offered for sale on the Alibaba marketplace.
incidents.impact: Personal information of about 500,000 people who voluntarily contributed medical and genetic data to the UK Biobank was found being offered for sale online.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — small group of AI hobbyists
incidents.vector: Use of leaked contractor credentials combined with guessing of internal Mythos operating endpoints on launch day.
incidents.impact: A group of AI hobbyists obtained access to Anthropic's private cybersecurity-focused Mythos agent on its launch day; Anthropic said no malicious prompts were issued and the access was used only to 'play around'.

incidents.victim: 35,000+ users across 13,000+ organizations in 26 countries (92% US)
incidents.industry: Multi-sector (healthcare, financial services, professional services, technology)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — credential theft / AiTM phishing
incidents.vector: Multi-stage phishing emails posing as internal 'code of conduct' compliance reviews used PDF attachments, Cloudflare CAPTCHAs and a chain of attacker-controlled .de domains to steer users into a Microsoft adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) sign-in flow that captured authentication tokens.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Research observed targeted theft of session tokens that bypass non-phishing-resistant MFA, hitting tens of thousands of users between 14-16 April with healthcare, financial-services and tech firms most affected.

incidents.victim: Industrial, consulting, retail and transportation organizations in India and Russia
incidents.vector: Tax-themed phishing emails impersonating Indian and Russian tax authorities deliver a Rust-based loader that pulls down ValleyRAT and the previously undocumented Python-based ABCDoor backdoor, which abuses pythonw.exe and Socket.IO over HTTPS to hide its remote-control traffic.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky logged 1,600+ malicious tax-themed messages in this campaign between early January and early February, with Silver Fox's first observed expansion into Russia and persistent surveillance capabilities including multi-monitor screen streaming, clipboard theft and remote input control.
